previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted with fever and tachycardia after being witnessed drinking water, posing a high aspiration risk. Initial concerns for infection led to brief antibiotic use, but clinical improvement and stable imaging supported a diagnosis of aspiration pneumonitis rather than pneumonia. Antibiotics were discontinued, and he remained afebrile for over 72 hours. Hypernatremia (sodium 152) was corrected with free water flushes via G-tube. A fourth recurrence of C. difficile was confirmed, requiring a prolonged vancomycin taper. His HIV remained well-controlled with an undetectable viral load and stable CD4 count. He was discharged to extended care on the vancomycin regimen, home medications, and hydration protocol.
